why: Doc quote is verbatim and the whole line is that one sentence (curl https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode.md, line 287, bullet under '### How backgrounding works'; neighbours at :286 cleanup-on-exit and :288 memory-pressure reaping do not reverse it). But the finding's OUR STATE is factually wrong and it names the wrong subsystem. (1) The two cited constants are real and say what was claimed - deferred-mcp-tools.ts:92 breaks the capability-search listing at MAX_DEFERRED_CAPABILITY_SEARCH_OUTPUT, sandbox.ts:276/:329-332 throws WorkflowEvaluationLimitError past DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES - but both belong to the deferred-tool search and the workflow sandbox, neither of which is the background shell. (2) 'the background-shell path has none' is false. The background shell is bash_background (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1402-1412, createBackgroundBashTool) -> requestSupervisedProcess({background:true}) -> ProcessSupervisor -> ProcessStore, and ProcessStore.append IS an output-byte ceiling: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-store.ts:7 'const MAX_LOG_BYTES = 64 * 1024' and :126-131 compute 'drop = max(0, combined.byteLength - limit)', rewrite the log to combined.subarray(drop) and advance baseCursor by the dropped byte count. Production uses the default with no override (SessionManager.ts:3573 'new ProcessStore({ root: join(SESSIONS_DIR, ".pi-processes") })'); the only maxLogBytes argument in the tree is a test at process-supervisor.test.ts:698. Two more ceilings on the same path the finding also missed: ProcessSupervisor.MAX_FOREGROUND_STREAM_BYTES = 64*1024 (process-supervisor.ts:28, applied by appendBoundedStream at :750-754) and OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES in orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-177. So 'the only output-byte ceilings in the tree are X and Y' is wrong on its own terms. (3) The CONSEQUENCE is handled one layer up, which is this repo's recurring false-positive shape. Claude needs a 5GB kill switch because it accumulates the full background-task output; here accumulation is structurally impossible - the on-disk log is a fixed 64 KiB rolling window, so a task that floods output writes 64 KiB forever and the cursor accounting (baseCursor/nextCursor, readLog at :142-148, surfaced to the model as next_offset via handlers/bash-output.ts and pi-agent.ts:6141 requestBashOutput) keeps the gap visible rather than silently lying. Termination is not absent either: BACKGROUND_PROCESS_MAX_LIFETIME_MS = 24h caps every background shell (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:952, applied at :1411 and :1590), and ProcessSupervisor.trackAppend (:675-681) SIGKILLs the whole process tree and marks the record 'lost' if the store write ever fails, which is the disk-exhaustion case the 5GB rule guards. The literal-number grep is a search for the wrong constant: verified binary-safe with grep -rain that no 5GB literal exists, which is true and irrelevant. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions), and not a rebrand/subscription-flow product difference. What survives is a much smaller and differently-worded residual, not the filed finding.
correctedState: The background-shell path DOES have an output-byte ceiling, and it is the ceiling the finding says is missing: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-store.ts:7 MAX_LOG_BYTES = 64 KiB, enforced in ProcessStore.append (:118-138) as a rolling window that drops the oldest bytes and advances baseCursor, used with the default by production (SessionManager.ts:3573). Two further caps sit on the same path: ProcessSupervisor.MAX_FOREGROUND_STREAM_BYTES = 64 KiB (process-supervisor.ts:28, :750-754) and OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES for subagent output (orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-177). Background tasks are also terminated on two axes: a 24h BACKGROUND_PROCESS_MAX_LIFETIME_MS (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:952, :1411, :1590) and an immediate SIGKILL of the process tree with status 'lost' if a log append fails (process-supervisor.ts:675-681). Because output never accumulates past 64 KiB, the resource-exhaustion harm Claude's 5GB rule prevents cannot occur here. The only true residual is a behavioural difference, not a missing ceiling: a runaway background task that floods output keeps running (up to 24h) with its excess output discarded, where Claude Code would kill it at 5GB and leave a stderr note; and the drop is signalled to the model only implicitly, through a next_offset that outruns the bytes returned, rather than by an explicit note. If that residual is worth filing, it should be filed as 'no explicit dropped-output note on BashOutput / no volume-triggered termination', citing process-store.ts:126-131, not as 'the background-shell path has no output-byte ceiling'.
